title.narrative: The Coalition for Integrity and Accountability - AMAN
The Coalition for Integrity and Accountability - AMAN

description.narrative:
AMAN's overall objective for the new strategy 2023-2025 is to hold power to account for the common good.
Strategic Objectives are:
SO1: Strengthening the integrity, transparency, accountability, and the anti-corruption system in the management of public funds and affairs and services provision.
SO2: Promoting integrity of the governance system and holding the political class accountable concerning their decisions for public interest.
SO3: Promoting community mobilization in support of anti-corruption efforts and holding the authority accountable.
SO4: Develop the institutional and organizational performance capacity of AMAN to meet its mission, vision and partnership relationship at national, international and Arab levels.

SO2: Främja integriteten i styrsystemet och hålla den politiska klassen ansvarig för sina beslut i allmänhetens intresse.
SO3: Främja samhällsmobilisering till stöd för antikorruptionsinsatser och hålla myndigheten ansvarig.
SO4: Utveckla AMAN:s institutionella och organisatoriska prestationsförmåga för att uppfylla dess uppdrag, vision och partnerskapsrelationer på nationell, internationell och arabisk nivå.

description.narrative:
The information below is based on annual reports and annual meetings.
The period was marked by on the one hand the war in Gaza, large-scale military operations in the northern West Bank, and a financial collapse in both the Gaza and the West Bank, and on the other hand a newly-appointed technocratic government in the PA tasked with implementing the PA's reform agenda. AMAN has expressed their initial optimism vis-a-vis the new government who seem, according to AMAN, to be open to reform and collaboration with civil society.
What have the operations led to?
AMAN has continued to engage in advocacy vis-a-vis the Palestinian government with a view to promote integrity, transparency and accountability. Although it is of course difficult to establish a causal line between civil society advocacy and government decisions. Nevertheless, during the period, the government took several steps that were in line with the recommendations made by AMAN through its advocacy. This includes the adoption of a cross-sectoral National Anti-corruption Strategy, several austerity measures aimed at rationalizing government expenditures, including regulating the movement and use of government vehicles, restricting travel missions and halting the purchase of new furniture and vehicles. In addition, the government implemented merit-based appointments for senior government positions, and increased efforts to enforce the halting of service extensions for employees over the legal retirement age.
AMAN has also engaged with local government units (i.e. municipal/village councils) by providing training in integrity and accountability during service delivery to local inhabitants, leading to the adoptions of integrity manual within 42 LGU's. Another important step undertaken by the government, which is in line with the recommendations of AMAN, was to grant local authorities the authority to collect property taxes and fines for non-payment.
Another highlight is AMAN's work on promoting community mobilization in support of anti-corruption efforts and holding power to account. AMAN has organized 80 different social accountability initiatives with the participation of over 200 people. These include twenty-five initiatives led by youth in the West Bank in Gaza which focused on the integrity and transparency in the distribution of humanitarian aid. AMAN also broadcasted over 10 000 radio spots across 21 stations in the West Bank to encourage citizens to report corruption. Included in this was a awareness raising campaign to promote the AMAN Advocacy and Legal Advice Center (ALAC), resulting in 264 legal consultations and 51 cases being adopted by ALAC related to corruption suspicions. A yearly survey undertaken by AMAN which asked the participants to answer whether they are willing to report suspicions of corruption without fear. This years number landed at 53 %, which is an improvement compared to last years figure of 50 %.
What has changed for whom?
As is mentioned above, it is not possible to establish a direct causal link between advocacy efforts from a civil society actor and a government decision, especially as the latter rarely explicitly acknowledges the impact of the former.
Nevertheless, AMAN is a long-standing and well-regarded actor within the area of anti-corruption and has a good working relationship with many government institutions. This, in combination with the overall impression that the new technocratic government of Palestine is genuinely open to reform, leads to the conclusion that it is not implausible that AMAN's advocacy work has had a genuine effect on the work of the government.
The advocacy that AMAN has engaged with vis-à-vis the new government comes at a time that is opportune given the willingness to reform, in combination with increasingly strong external pressure on the PA to undertake its reform agenda, not least from the EU. Given that PA reform is also highlighted as a key factor in the future establishment of a sovereign Palestinian state, most recently in the New York Declaration of 28 July 2025, supporting the efforts of the reform agenda can have effects that go far beyond mere policy reform.
Specifically, the above mentioned decisions by the government undertaken, potentially as a result of AMAN's advocacy, work towards Expenditure Policy Management which is a key component in the reform agenda and in balancing the PA's budget in a very difficult financial situation. The adoption of the Cross-sectoral national anti-corruption strategy is another step in the reform agenda specifically, and the combatting of corruption in general.
In a similar vein, the empowerment of LGUs in the area of taxation is an important step in the efforts to decentralize power in Palestine which has the potential in the long-term to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of public service delivery and promote local economic development. These efforts are also in line with the New York Declarations recommendation to support the PA's decentralisation agenda.
Finally, we can conclude that AMAN's efforts to raise awareness and strengthen the capacity of government officials, civil society organizations and the general public have increased public awareness of corruption and increased the number of people who can report cases of corruption without fear.
